$comment: facts@2 (graph-store plan 0.1, T5a.1; design §2a, GS15). The fact relations circle-ir owes the store, as Arrow columns in canonical order keyed by ids@0.1. The successor of facts@1, published as a major in one step (P1 of the facts@2 decision of 2026-11-02, P1-P7): site positions relative to the enclosing declaration's start line, no site_file, declaration positions in decl_pos (P2, layout V3); a stable file key in every relation that names a file, superseding the dense file_id of reconciliation decision 2 (P3); the relations and columns the T6 rules read (P4); decl_pos and parse_error store-only (P5). Deferred and not in this file (P6): registration_bound, the TypeScript-only relations, imports.is_static, the entries route method and path. Everything facts@1 fixed and P1-P7 do not change stays: 128-bit ids, sets with no nulls, the total canonical order, fixed-size chunks, the producer's metadata keys, hex digests. This file is the schema the store reads; the TypeScript mirror is src/facts/schema2.ts and tests/facts/schema2.test.ts locks the two together. facts@1 (schemas/facts@1.json) stays the producer's default until the store has adopted facts@2.

id_encoding.$comment: An ids@0.1 id is 128 bits printed as 26 lowercase base32 characters (RFC 4648, unpadded). In a column it is the 16 raw bytes, so every id column is FixedSizeBinary(16); the 2 trailing padding bits of the printed form are always zero. Node ids (the flow endpoints) and file keys have the same width: see node_id and file_key.

node_id.$comment: The fixed-width form of an ids@0.1 node id (stable-ids design decision 1a, adopted 2026-11-01): digest128 over the parts listed, i.e. BLAKE3 of the UTF-8 parts each followed by NUL, first 16 bytes - the same construction as every other ids@0.1 id, printed as 26 base32 characters where a printed form is needed. body_id is the printed body id of the innermost declaration whose body encloses the node (<decl id>.<body_hash>, 53 characters; after the snapshot's #n re-key where decl applied one); kind is the IR array the node comes from; ordinal counts the nodes of that kind inside that body in IR array order, from 0, in decimal without leading zeros. It is a function of the printed node id <body_id>/<tag><ordinal> (tags b, d, u, c) and nothing else: an edit to one body re-keys only that body's nodes. The example is a test vector (tests/facts/schema2.test.ts recomputes it).

file_key.$comment: The stable file key (P3; the ids@0.1 file kind of the stable-ids plan): digest128 over the parts listed - BLAKE3 of the UTF-8 parts each followed by NUL, first 16 bytes, the construction of every other ids@0.1 id. path is the file's files.path exactly as written (repository-relative, /-separated). The key is a function of the path and nothing else: adding or removing a file adds or removes only that file's rows, and moving one re-keys only that file's rows. It replaces facts@1's dense, snapshot-local file_id, and no delta re-maps through files.path. Every relation that names a file carries it as the column file (fixed16): files, decl, imports, parse_error. files is keyed by file, so two paths with one key (a 128-bit collision) fail the producer's key check rather than merge. The example is a test vector (tests/facts/schema2.test.ts recomputes it).

positions.$comment: Layout V3 (P2). A site (call, unresolved, ref, registration) carries rel_line = the site's line minus the start line (decl_pos.line) of the declaration whose body holds it (caller_id or from_id), and col; it carries no file, since its file is that declaration's file. A site never lies above its declaration's start, so rel_line fits u32. Declaration positions live only in decl_pos. No rule needs an absolute line: rendering one is decl_pos.line + rel_line, a single join. A blast radius seeds from decl changes only (a body added, removed or changed), never from site rows: an edit that adds or removes comment or blank lines inside a body moves rel_line below it while body_hash stays the same.

types.$comment: The closed set of column types. `dict` is Dictionary<Int8 index, Utf8 value> over a fixed vocabulary listed on the column; the whole vocabulary is written as the dictionary, in the listed order, whether or not every value occurs.

canonical_order.$comment: Within a relation rows are sorted ascending by the key columns in key order, then by every remaining column in schema order, so the comparator is total and a relation has one byte form. Column orders: fixed16 by unsigned bytes; u32 numerically; utf8 and dict by Unicode code point (which equals UTF-8 byte order), never by UTF-16 code unit or dictionary index; bool false before true; null before every value (a dead branch: no column is nullable). Relations are sets: after the sort exact duplicate rows are dropped and counted (manifest duplicates_dropped per relation), so rows are strictly increasing and a store may refuse equal rows.

chunking.$comment: After the canonical sort a relation is cut into record batches of chunk_rows rows each (the last one shorter); a relation with no rows has no record batch. One Arrow IPC file per relation, so the batch boundaries are part of the bytes. Fixed row-count chunks, not file ranges: nine of the twelve relations are not keyed by a file.

loading.$comment: Every relation states store_only (P5). A store_only relation is written to the snapshot, digested into the snapshot digest and read back for rendering like any other, but a store does not load it into the engine unless a rule names it (decl_pos has one row per declaration and no rule reads it). Every other relation is loaded.
loading.store_only: written, digested and read; loaded into the engine only when a rule names it
loading.engine: every relation whose store_only is false

metadata.$comment: Schema-level custom metadata, and nothing else (no timestamps, no host): facts (the value facts@2, never a -draft) and ids always; engine and parser when the caller names them. The producer's manifest.json beside the files repeats them and adds source, chunk_rows and per relation file, rows, batches, bytes, blake3 (file-byte digest, hex) and duplicates_dropped.

columns.name: file
columns.doc: The stable file key: digest128(["ids@0.1", "file", path]) (file_key).

columns.name: path
columns.doc: Repository-relative, /-separated.

columns.name: content_hash
columns.doc: blake3 of the file's UTF-8 bytes, first 16 bytes.

columns.name: partial
columns.doc: The file did not parse cleanly (the engine's partial): its call sites may be missing, so its declarations and what they reach are may-be-live and an answer that relies on absence is not final. A partial file has exactly one parse_error row.

decl.doc: One row per declaration, with no position (declaration positions are in decl_pos). That every declaration loads its module is not a column: it follows from file and the module row of that file (kind module).

columns.name: id
columns.doc: ids@0.1 declaration id. Unique per snapshot: when two files derive the same id (two package-info.java of one package in different bundles), the later one in file order takes the stable-ids #n suffix on its qualified_name and the id derived from it, as the ids@0.1 duplicate rule does within one scope.

columns.name: name
columns.doc: The declaration's own name as ids@0.1 records it (e.g. <clinit>; default for an anonymous default export). An unresolved site in a reached body can bind to a declaration of the same name.

columns.name: signature
columns.doc: The ids@0.1 canonical signature as written; empty for modules and types without type parameters.

columns.name: file
columns.doc: The declaring file's key (file_key).

columns.name: parent_id
columns.doc: The enclosing declaration's id (ids@0.1 parent), rewritten by the snapshot's #n re-key as caller_id is; all-zero bytes for a module, which has none (no nulls in facts@2).

columns.name: body_hash
columns.doc: ids@0.1 body hash; all-zero bytes when the engine derived none (no nulls in facts@2; Java always derives one).

columns.name: type_only
columns.doc: Used only as a type (the engine's typeOnly): left out of reach and dead-code answers.

columns.name: anonymous
columns.doc: The ids@0.1 flag unstable:anonymous: an anonymous or nested body keyed by its enclosing declaration plus its structural position there; an edit to the enclosing body may re-key it.

columns.name: duplicate
columns.doc: The ids@0.1 flag unstable:duplicate: the id carries a #n suffix, so inserting a same-named declaration before it re-keys it.

columns.name: contained
columns.doc: A strong contains edge from parent_id to this declaration, computed by the producer: whenever the parent runs, this declaration is in use (a nested or anonymous body, a module's top-level value, a type's field or <clinit>, a constructor outside Java; a Java constructor runs only when called). False for a module.

columns.name: loads_parent
columns.doc: A strong loads edge from this declaration to parent_id, computed by the producer: running this declaration initializes its parent (Java: true for every declaration that is not a type and whose parent is a type; the rows java-graph's loads holds).

decl_pos.doc: Declaration positions, out of decl so that a line shift changes no row a rule reads (P2). One row per decl row. Store-only (P5): read for rendering, SARIF, and mapping a diff hunk or a finding's line to its declaration; site lines are relative to line.

columns.name: id
columns.doc: The decl id.

columns.name: line
columns.doc: 1-based start line.

columns.name: end_line
columns.doc: 1-based end line, inclusive.

columns.name: col
columns.doc: 0-based start column.

columns.name: end_col
columns.doc: 0-based end column.

call.doc: Key: the site as (caller, relative line, column) maps one-to-one onto facts@1's (site_file, site_line, site_col), since the site's file is the caller's file; every row facts@1's key told apart stays apart.

columns.name: caller_id
columns.doc: The enclosing declaration (the module's id for top-level code).

columns.name: callee_id
columns.doc: The declaration that can run; one row per candidate body on polymorphic.

columns.name: method_name
columns.doc: The name as written at the site (new sites: the class name). A site names more than one call in a chained expression, and the name is what tells them apart.

columns.name: rel_line
columns.doc: The site's line minus the caller's decl_pos.line (positions).

columns.name: col
columns.doc: The site's column, 0-based.

columns.name: declaring
columns.doc: True on a polymorphic row whose callee is the member the receiver's static type declares (java-graph's declaring target); the navigation index's via for the other rows of that call (same caller_id, rel_line, col and method_name) is that row's callee_id. False on every other row, every exact and inferred row included.

unresolved.doc: Key: the site and the name as written, plus receiver and reason, because one site and name can carry several rows that differ only in those (T4, 2026-11-01). caller_id takes site_file's place in the key: the site's file is the caller's file.

columns.name: receiver
columns.doc: The library type the call lands on; empty when unknown (no nulls in facts@2).

columns.name: rel_line
columns.doc: The site's line minus the caller's decl_pos.line (positions).

columns.name: col
columns.doc: The site's column, 0-based.

ref.doc: A declaration used as a value - passed, stored, returned (the engine's references; Java method references): it may run, nothing proves it does. A weak edge for reach. Key: the site first (from_id, rel_line, col), then to_id, as call, unresolved and registration key their sites.

columns.name: from_id
columns.doc: The declaration whose body holds the reference.

columns.name: to_id
columns.doc: The declaration referenced.

columns.name: rel_line
columns.doc: The site's line minus from_id's decl_pos.line (positions).

columns.name: col
columns.doc: The site's column, 0-based.

registration.doc: A registration the recognizers saw but could not tie to a declaration (the engine's unresolvedRegistrations, #1092). Reach counts it only when from_id's body is reached.

columns.name: from_id
columns.doc: The declaration whose body holds the site (Java: the engine's from, always known since #1092; otherwise the innermost declaration enclosing the site, the module's id for top-level code).

columns.name: evidence
columns.doc: The engine's evidence line.

columns.name: rel_line
columns.doc: The site's line minus from_id's decl_pos.line (positions).

columns.name: col
columns.doc: The site's column, 0-based.

parse_error.doc: Where a partial file stopped parsing: its first blocking error in source order (the engine's parseError). Exactly one row per files row with partial true, and none for any other. Store-only (P5).

columns.name: file
columns.doc: The partial file's key (file_key).

columns.name: line
columns.doc: 1-based.

columns.name: col
columns.doc: 0-based (the engine's 1-based parse-error column minus one).

columns.name: node_kind
columns.doc: ERROR for a region the grammar could not read, or MISSING <token> for a token the parser had to insert.

columns.name: parent_kind
columns.doc: The syntax node the error sits in.

flow.doc: Def-use and taint edges on ids@0.1 node ids in their fixed-width form (node_id). The java-graph@0.1 post-pass writes one def-use row per DFG use with a reaching definition in the same file: from_id = the definition's node id (kind def), to_id = the use's node id (kind use); data flows from from_id to to_id. taint rows are not written by the post-pass yet (the engine's taint flows are line-keyed, not node-keyed); the kind stays in the vocabulary for them.

columns.name: file
columns.doc: The importing file's key (file_key).

columns.name: target
columns.doc: The imported name as written, without a trailing `.*`; a static import's member path for `import static`.

columns.name: wildcard
columns.doc: In the key: one file may import both X and X.*, which share target.

columns.name: kind
columns.doc: entry-index@0.1 kinds plus the design's data-declared kinds; the engine's `bean` is written as `di` (one meaning, one word).

columns.name: source
columns.doc: What declared the entry — the annotation, the supertype member, the manifest or file; the engine's evidence line.

moved.doc: Moves and renames between two snapshots: facts, not delete + insert. Empty from a single-snapshot post-pass.
